title: Elkéstem, Elveszítettem: New Verbs for a Bad Day

sections.title: Two new past-tense verbs
sections.content: You already know késik ("to be late, to run late") from Unit 15's travel problems — elkésik adds el- to mean "to be late for something and miss it": Elkéstem a munkából means "I was late for work" (and it cost me something). elveszít ("to lose something") is a brand new regular verb — despite looking similar to vesz ("to buy") from Unit 25, the two are unrelated and conjugate completely differently. elveszít takes a direct object, so it splits into indefinite and definite past exactly like lát does.

items.english: This morning I was late for work.
I lost my key in the park.

sections.content: elveszítettem looks nothing like vettem, even though vesz and veszít can sound alike to a new ear — vesz means "buy", veszít means "lose", and they run on completely different stems (vett- vs. veszít-). Keep the two apart.
